Bond Maturity: $1.5 billion bond maturity for Hughes Corporation due August 1, 2026.

Bankruptcy Filing: Chapter 11 filed for Hughes entities; excludes EchoStar Corporation, other non-Hughes subsidiaries, and Hughes international entities.

Release Date: August 03, 2026

For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript.

Positive Points

Strive Inc (NASDAQ:ASST) has a strong cash position of $14-15 billion after closing the AT&T transaction, providing significant financial flexibility.

The company holds 261.8 million SpaceX shares, a valuable asset that could appreciate further and provide substantial liquidity.

Strive Inc (NASDAQ:ASST) increased its share buyback authorization to $5 billion, signaling confidence in its own value and a commitment to returning capital to shareholders.

The company has a solid spectrum portfolio (AWS-3, CBRS, 700 MHz) that could be monetized, with potential for participation in future spectrum auctions.

Strive Inc (NASDAQ:ASST) is pivoting towards AI and restructuring to capitalize on the paradigm shift, which could drive future growth and efficiency.

Negative Points

Strive Inc (NASDAQ:ASST) faces a $5-7 billion tax liability related to the SpaceX transaction and wireless network termination, which could strain finances.

The company's Boost Mobile business has been treading water for four years, losing subscribers and struggling to compete effectively.

Strive Inc (NASDAQ:ASST) is entangled in litigation with tower companies, which has stalled negotiations and increased costs, leading to bankruptcy filings for Hughes and DISH Wireless.

There are restrictions in bond indentures that currently prevent the company from buying back stock, limiting its ability to capitalize on its discounted valuation.

Strive Inc (NASDAQ:ASST) is cautious about the frothy market and may be slow to deploy capital, potentially missing opportunities to create shareholder value.

He noted bond indenture restrictions currently limit repurchases.

Today's big story: Nvidia Added $954 Billion In A Day. Is Jensen Huang Too Big To Fire?

T-Mobile US stock closed at $166.36 on Monday, November 23. That is 24.1% below its highest close of the past year, which was $219.11 on March 6.

Over the past year, the shares lost 19.3%, with dividends included. The S&P 500 returned 12% over the same dates. Since its low of $146.54 on October 23, the stock has returned 13.5%.

Our read: the clearest route higher is home internet, sold over T-Mobile's 5G network and over fiber lines. Its full size does not show in the reported numbers yet. To judge it, start with why the stock trades where it does.

T-Mobile Stock Trades Below The Market's Multiple

T-Mobile trades at 15.8 times its earnings over the last four quarters. That ratio is the price-to-earnings multiple, or P/E. The S&P 500, taken as one company, trades at 21.2 times.

At the end of September, T-Mobile's P/E was 15.5. It was lower at only 4 of the 40 quarter ends since late 2016.

T-Mobile's P/E of 15.5 at the end of September was lower at only 4 of the 40 quarter ends since late 2016. If you hold the stock while you wait for a higher price, your savings could still bring in steady income. The Trefis Income Solution pays a dividend yield about 3 times the S&P 500's, from 50 companies that have paid dividends for at least 10 years in a row. See what it pays.

Slowing growth is part of the reason for the lower P/E. Revenue grew 11.3% in the quarter to December 2025, against a year earlier. Growth then slowed each quarter, to 10.6%, 7.9% and 7.4% in the quarter to September.

Management tied part of that to the timing of acquisitions a year earlier, including the close of U.S. Cellular. Debt adds weight too. Total debt was $118 billion at the end of September. That equals 66.3% of the stock's market value, against 20.2% for the S&P 500.

What Is T-Mobile's Home Internet Opportunity?

T-Mobile sells home internet in two ways. One runs over its 5G phone network and is called fixed wireless. The other runs over fiber lines. On the October 28 call, management said it was "tracking really well ahead of pace to our goal of hitting 15 million customers by 2030" in fixed wireless.

Fiber is the newer of the two. Management said the fiber business had "approximately 20% 12-month penetration." Penetration is the share of homes reached that became customers. Management also said it was "well on track" toward its "target of 3 million to 4 million customers by 2030." The fixed wireless and fiber goals are both 2030 targets, and their outcome is not yet known.

Is Cheap Verizon Stock A Real Bargain?

Today's big story: Nvidia Added $954 Billion In A Day. Is Jensen Huang Too Big To Fire?

Verizon Communications stock trades at 11.8 times its profit over the last four quarters. That ratio, called the P/E, is the price paid for each dollar of yearly profit. It sits 44.5% below the median S&P 500 company's P/E of 21.2.

The stock returned 21.5% including dividends in the year from Nov 20, 2025, against 12% for the S&P 500. It closed at $46.45 on Monday. So is this a sound business on sale, or a fair price for one that has stopped growing?

On the figures, it looks more like a real bargain, as long as the cash holds up. Verizon's cash covers its dividend with room to spare. Its margin dip comes from one weak quarter. The risk is debt almost as large as its market value.

Why does Verizon look cheap?

Free cash flow, the cash left after paying for the network, was $17.9 billion in the four quarters to September, down from $20.6 billion a year earlier. Verizon paid $11.7 billion in dividends and $4 billion for buybacks in those quarters. At Monday's close, the dividend equals 6.1% of the share price a year.

Verizon hands its owners 6.1% of the share price each year in cash. If you live on that money, you need it to keep arriving even when the stock falls. The Trefis Income Solution pays a dividend yield about 3 times the S&P 500's, from 50 companies that have paid dividends for at least 10 years in a row. See what it pays.

Free cash flow also equals 9.3% of Verizon's market value. Most of Verizon's revenue comes from household phone and internet bills. Its Consumer unit brought in 77.3% of revenue in 2025.

What does the longer record show?

Growth is the fair case against the stock. Verizon's revenue grew 1.4% in the four quarters to September. The median S&P 500 company grew 8.7%. AT&T grew 3.5% and T-Mobile US grew 9.3% over their own latest four quarters.

Operating margin is the share of sales left after running costs. The latest 20.9% sits below the three-period average of 21.5%, which includes it. A year earlier it was 23%.

One quarter drives that drop. In the three months to December 2025, the margin was 13.8%. The next three quarters ran at 23.9%, 21% and 25.2%.

Debt is the other reason the market may be right. Verizon owed $189 billion at the end of September. That is 97.9% of its market value, against 20.2% for the S&P 500 taken as one company. The price appears to assume this debt could weigh on what owners get back.

Released: The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income. It is a free guide from Fisher Investments covering what your retirement will really cost, where the cash flow should come from, and how much you can safely withdraw each year. Learn more here. Learn More Here › (sponsor)

A dividend can only last as long as the cash behind it. When a company has to borrow to cover the gap between what it gets and what it pays out, the dividend is effectively being paid with lenders' money. Pfizer (NYSE:PFE) yields 6.25%, but its free cash flow yield is only 5.81%. It is one of three well-known income names whose payouts lean on debt more than they should.

Marko Aliaksandr / Shutterstock.com

The quick test: a dividend holds up when the cash measure that matches the business covers it with room to spare. For most companies, that measure is free cash flow. For REITs, the better gauge is FFO. If borrowing has to fill the gap, every dollar taken on brings interest that competes with the next dividend check, and that game lasts only as long as lenders keep saying yes.

Medical Properties Trust (MPT): A 13% Yield Financed at 9.25%

Medical Properties Trust (NYSE:MPT) is a hospital REIT whose shares now trade under the symbol MPT. It pays $0.09 per share each quarter, which works out to roughly 13% at the $2.76 share price on the day it filed its third-quarter results. That price was down from $4.70 at the second-quarter filing, a drop of about 41%. The yield is high because the stock collapsed. The payout did not grow.

Tutor Perini Corporation (TPC) Is a Trending Stock: Facts to Know Before Betting on It

Tutor Perini (TPC) has recently been on Zacks.com's list of the most searched stocks. Therefore, you might want to consider some of the key factors that could influence the stock's performance in the near future.

Over the past month, shares of this construction company have returned +18.3%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -10.2% change. During this period, the Zacks Building Products - Heavy Construction industry, which Tutor Perini falls in, has lost 14.4%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.

Earnings Estimate Revisions

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

Our analysis is essentially based on how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to take the latest business trends into account. When earnings estimates for a company go up, the fair value for its stock goes up as well. And when a stock's fair value is higher than its current market price, investors tend to buy the stock, resulting in its price moving upward. Because of this, empirical studies indicate a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and short-term stock price movements.

Tutor Perini is expected to post earnings of $1.33 per share for the current quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +24.3%. Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed +3.5%.

The consensus earnings estimate of $5.67 for the current fiscal year indicates a year-over-year change of +32.2%. This estimate has changed +11.9% over the last 30 days.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $6.1 indicates a change of +7.7% from what Tutor Perini is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has remained unchanged.

Having a strong externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool, the Zacks Rank, offers a more conclusive picture of a stock's price direction in the near term, since it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. Due to the size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, Tutor Perini is rated Zacks Rank #2 (Buy).
